subject: Life Skills
title: Hotel Room Safety Check
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Hotel Room Safety Check.

hook.text: A frequent traveler checks three things within 60 seconds of entering any hotel room. It has become automatic.

buildup.text: First: locate the nearest fire exit and count doors between your room and the stairwell. Smoke blocks visibility.

discovery.text: Second: test the deadbolt and chain. If the door does not close securely, request a different room immediately.

twist.text: Third: check for hidden cameras near clocks, smoke detectors, and mirrors. A phone flashlight reveals lens reflections.

climax.text: Keep your room number private. If the front desk says it aloud, ask for a new room. Discretion is basic safety.

punchline.text: Sixty seconds at check-in. Peace of mind all night.

quiz.question: What should you do if the front desk announces your room number loudly?
options: Ignore it since hotel lobbies are safe
Ask for a different room to maintain privacy
Tell nearby guests to forget the number
